concrete_scene.heading: Worked protected computation: the enclave is valid, the fallback leaks
concrete_scene.actor_or_system: A protected model service, a valid enclave attestation, an encoded-computation proof, a latency budget, an ordinary fallback worker, a consumer, and leakage channels
concrete_scene.attempted_action: Treat correct output and valid protected-path evidence as end-to-end confidentiality after silent unprotected fallback.
concrete_scene.observable_outcome: The transaction rejects because prompt and state crossed an unauthorized boundary; even protected execution retains timing, length, purpose, and side-channel residuals.
concrete_scene.failed_or_tested_boundary: The scene tests whether component attestation substitutes for transaction authorization, semantic correctness, or end-to-end privacy; it does not.
concrete_scene.residual_owner: Adversary, asset, trust-anchor, attestation, proof, verifier, freshness, leakage, fallback, authorization, performance, privacy, and cost owners retain residuals.
concrete_scene.evidence_boundary: The finite review checks typed evidence and fallback routes and does not establish cryptographic soundness, hardware trust, side-channel resistance, authorization, privacy, or acceptable cost.

worked_trace.heading: Worked protected computation: the enclave is valid, the fallback leaks
worked_trace.maximum_inference: Evidence types, leakage lists, scope invalidation, and fallback authorization can be separated in the finite model; cryptography, hardware, side channels, semantics, authorization, privacy, and cost remain unproven.

counterexample_or_simpler_baseline: The enclave-only baseline treats valid attestation as end-to-end protection. The compositional contract includes fallback, metadata, purpose, authorization, leakage, and disclosure.
readable_claim: An attested enclave can prove which code ran while the overall service still leaks through inputs, outputs, metadata, fallback, or an unauthorized purpose.
normative_rule: Compose confidentiality, integrity, proof statement, trust anchors, freshness, leakage channels, verifier policy, authorization, observable fallback, revocation, and cost at the transaction boundary. Reject any unprotected fallback unless separately authorized and disclosed; never let attestation imply semantic correctness or end-to-end privacy.

formal_binding.anchor: compositional execution contract that names the adversary

caveat_consolidation.local_caveat: The scene states once that the finite review assumes its cryptographic and hardware fields.
caveat_consolidation.consolidated_disposition: Adversaries, assets, leakage, cryptography, attestations, hardware, verifiers, freshness, authorization, fallback, semantics, privacy, cost, support, and release remain distinct.

bookkeeping_surface_disposition: The valid enclave and leaking fallback stay reader-facing; complete trust and leakage matrices remain formal.

editorial_diagnostics.mega_sentence_disposition: The reader claim gives protected computation a component/end-to-end boundary.
editorial_diagnostics.hedge_disposition: The cryptographic and hardware limitations follow the concrete fallback once.
editorial_diagnostics.table_disposition: Primitive and guarantee tables remain because confidentiality, integrity, proof, authorization, and privacy differ.

non_claims: The scene does not establish cryptographic soundness or hardware trust.
Valid attestation does not establish authorization, semantic correctness, or end-to-end privacy.
The editorial revision does not move support or release state.
